t:
(a) Extension of Certification.—Paragraph (2) of section 128(a) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2217) is amended by striking “a reference to March” and inserting “a reference to September”. 
    (b) Required Authority.—Such section 128 is further amended by adding at the end the following:“(e) Required Authority.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, with respect to a multiyear contract entered into under subsection (a), this section shall be deemed to meet the requirements under subsection (i)(3) and (l)(3) of section 2306b of title 10, United States Code.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "Certification" and "multiyear contract" signal a process involving outside parties such as contractors. In fact the section only changes a certification deadline date and deems the statutory requirements for multiyear contract authority to be met. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal entities, or right to sue, and entering into a contract is not participation in a federal decision.
fable.s: this section shall be deemed to meet the requirements under subsection (i)(3) and (l)(3) of section 2306b of title 10, United States Code

qwen_block.w: This section amends statutory deadlines and legal authorities regarding multiyear contracts. It does not involve consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities such as the public, states, or private organizations. The text deals entirely with internal federal legal requirements and administrative timelines.

opus.w: The section changes a certification deadline from March to September and treats the existing section as meeting the multiyear-contracting requirements of 10 U.S.C. 2306b. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. Any certification involved stays inside the federal government, and a contractor holding a multiyear contract is not taking part in the decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends statutory deadlines and legal requirements for multiyear contracts. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from parties outside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes applications for contracts, and this text merely adjusts the legal framework for such contracts without creating a participatory process for outsiders.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Extension of Certification.—Paragraph (2) of section 128(a) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2217) is amended by striking “a reference to March” and inserting “a reference to September”. (b) Required Authority.—Such section 128 is further amended by adding at the end the following:“(e) Required Authority.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, with respect to a multiyear contract entered into under subsection (a), this section shall be deemed to meet the requirements under subsection (i)(3) and (l)(3) of section 2306b of title 10, United States Code.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "multiyear contract" implies negotiation with outside contractors, which is a form of participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for contracts and licenses. Furthermore, this section merely amends statutory references and deems certain requirements met; it does not establish a process for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in a decision. The actors involved are Congress (amending the law) and the executive branch (entering contracts), all of which are inside the federal government or excluded by the definition.
